summary: Built a system-level schematic of a row CDU with duty/standby electronic pumps, a brazed plate heat exchanger, filtration, expansion tank, instrumentation and individual rack isolation branches. Animated facility-water and glycol circuits connect the CDU to the rack cold-plate arrays through supply/return headers and quick couplings. Four modes demonstrate normal operation, standby-pump changeover, rack leak isolation and warm-water cooling. Numbered hotspots support component inspection, while staged narration follows heat collection and rejection. Geometry uses illustrative component proportions, not fabrication dimensions. Performance is a steady-state, lumped-parameter estimate using the specified coolant properties, design temperature differences, fixed hydraulic resistance and assumed pump efficiency. Warm-water operation raises rack inlet temperature; transient thermal ride-through and valve sizing are not simulated.

prompt: Build an interactive system model (system-level schematic) of a 1.2 MW row-level CDU (coolant distribution unit) for an AI data centre: the secondary side feeds 8 liquid-cooled racks of 150 kW each (25 % propylene-glycol water, 32 °C supply); each rack connects through supply/return manifolds, quick couplings and an isolating electronic water valve to the GPU cold plates inside. Inside the CDU: brazed plate heat exchanger, two variable-speed electronic water pumps (N+1, one duty one standby), filter, expansion/make-up tank, supply/return temperature, pressure and flow sensors. The primary side is facility chilled water (18 °C supply) with an electronic proportional valve modulating primary flow to hold the secondary supply temperature. Implement four switchable modes: ① normal operation; ② pump 1 failure → automatic changeover to the standby pump; ③ rack 5 leak → its branch valve isolates while the other racks keep running; ④ warm-water cooling with 32 °C primary supply. Requirements: animated primary/secondary loop flow in distinct colours, mode buttons, numbered component hotspots mapped to product categories (electronic water pump, electronic water valve, plate heat exchanger, liquid-cooling cold plate …), staged narration (rack heat pickup → return collection → plate-HX exchange → primary heat rejection → supply distribution), and computed total heat load, secondary flow and supply/return ΔT, plate-HX approach temperature, pump hydraulic power and its share of IT load.
